qAndA.answer: Hemlocks have alternate branching (branches emerge on alternating sides of the stem), while balsam firs have opposite branching (branches emerge directly across from each other on the stem).
qAndA.question: How does the hiker distinguish between a hemlock and a balsam fir based on their branching patterns?

qAndA.answer: The distinctive white bark with horizontal markings makes a birch tree easily recognizable, even without leaves.

youtube_description:
On my hikes in Southern Ontario near the place I live in, I like to stop and try to identify the trees around me.  Some of these are very basic id, and I am still learning as much as I can.  
In this video I was able to id the following trees:
-Pines (Red pines mostly, I think)
-Eastern Hemlock
-White Oak
-Black Spruce
-White Birch (also called Paper Birch)
This is part of Simcoe County Forests, by the Willow Creek in Midhurst/Springwater.
Hope you like this video, and if I made any mistakes, please please let me know.
